title: Is Vinyl Plank a Good Choice for Sammamish's Wet Climate?
meta: Yes, vinyl plank handles Sammamish rain, mud and dogs better than any wood floor. What matters is the moisture under it and the core you pick. Wills Flooring.
keywords: vinyl plank flooring wet climate, is vinyl plank good for rainy areas, vinyl plank humidity problems, best flooring for Pacific Northwest rain, vinyl plank flooring Sammamish WA

blocks.lead: Yes. Vinyl plank is the best-suited hard floor for Sammamish weather, because the plank itself cannot absorb water, swell or rot. The two things that can still go wrong, moisture rising from the crawlspace or slab and planks expanding in a sun-heated room, are install decisions, not reasons to avoid it.
blocks.detail: We install vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft for labor, with a 500 sq ft minimum. On the plateau most of the extra cost sits in the prep, and that is where wet-climate problems actually start.

blocks.html: Sammamish gets about 45 inches of rain a year, most of it walked into the house between October and April by kids, dogs and whoever was out at the Pine Lake fields. A typical Klahanie or Trossachs home has 1990s builder oak on the main floor, and by now a lot of it is gray at the back door and cupped near the dishwasher. So the real question is: if I replace it, will vinyl plank hold up any better? It will, for specific reasons, and it can fail for specific reasons too.

blocks.text: What 'waterproof' does and does not cover

items.title: Covered: water on top
items.text: Rain off a coat, a wet dog, a dishwasher leak found the next morning. The plank is vinyl over a stone or foamed core; it does not absorb water. Wipe it up and there is no swelling, no gray boards, no finish damage.

items.title: Not covered: water from below
items.text: Vinyl plank does not breathe. Moisture rising from a damp crawlspace or an unsealed slab gets trapped under it, where it feeds mold on the subfloor and lifts click joints. The plank survives; the house underneath does not.

items.title: Not covered: heat expansion
items.text: Vinyl moves with temperature more than humidity. A south-facing family room can swing 30°F between a February morning and a July afternoon. Rigid core planks with proper expansion gaps handle it; cheap flexible planks pinned under an island do not.

items.title: Not covered: seams under standing water
items.text: A floating floor is waterproof plank by plank, not as a sealed membrane. Water that sits for days can find a seam and reach the subfloor. A burst supply line still means lifting the floor to dry underneath.

blocks.text: When vinyl plank is the wrong answer

items.html: The crawlspace is actively wet. No floor fixes a drainage problem. If the plywood reads over 16 percent we will not install anything; spend on the crawlspace first.

The existing oak is sound and just tired. If your builder oak is flat, dry and simply gray at the doors, a sand and refinish at $3.99 per sq ft keeps real wood and usually costs less than plank plus tear-out.

You are selling a high-end Sahalee or Pine Lake home soon. Buyers at that price point still expect hardwood in the main living areas. Plank in the mudroom and lower level is fine; on the main floor it can cost you at resale.
The room is a true sunroom with unshaded south glass. Even rigid core has limits above about 100°F surface temperature. Tile or hardwood is safer there.

blocks.title: The failure we see most on the plateau:
blocks.text: A floating plank floor installed tight to the walls and pinned under a kitchen island, in a great room with a south-facing slider. The first hot week in July it peaks at the seams. It was not the rain. See why vinyl plank buckles or gaps in Sammamish.
What to check before you sign for vinyl plank

items: Ask for the subfloor moisture reading in writing, and what happens if it is high.
Choose a rigid core plank with at least a 20 mil wear layer for main floors and mudrooms.
Confirm expansion gaps at every wall and that the island sits on the subfloor, not on the plank.
Ask whether the underlayment is attached to the plank; loose foam can hold moisture.
Plan the transitions at exterior doors so water and grit stop at the threshold.
Get the 1-year workmanship warranty and the manufacturer's waterproof warranty in the same written quote.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank swell or warp in a humid climate?
faq.a: The plank itself does not absorb moisture, so humidity alone will not swell it. What moves vinyl is temperature. In a Sammamish house kept between 60 and 75°F it stays flat. Problems come from sun-heated rooms without expansion gaps, or from a damp subfloor underneath, both of which are prevented at install.

faq.q: Do I need a vapor barrier under vinyl plank over a crawlspace?
faq.a: Usually not on top of a dry plywood subfloor, since most rigid planks have an attached pad. The vapor barrier that matters is the one on the crawlspace dirt below. We check the plywood moisture with a pin meter at the estimate; if it is high, the crawlspace needs attention before any floor goes down.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank better than hardwood for a house with dogs and rain?
faq.a: For durability against water and mud, yes. Vinyl plank shrugs off wet paws and dries with a towel, while hardwood grays and cups at the doors over time. Hardwood still wins on resale in higher-priced Sammamish neighborhoods, which is why many families do plank in the mudroom and lower level and keep wood upstairs.

faq.q: How much does it cost to put vinyl plank in a whole Sammamish main floor?
faq.a: Installation labor is $2.50 per sq ft. A 1,400 sq ft main floor is 1,400 × $2.50 = $3,500 in labor, plus the plank you choose, any tear-out of the old floor and subfloor prep. Those are quoted at the free in-home estimate after we measure and test the subfloor.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank go over my existing builder-grade oak?
faq.a: Sometimes. If the oak is flat, dry, nailed tight and not cupped, a rigid core plank can float over it. Cupped or squeaky boards need to be flattened or removed first, since vinyl plank will show every ridge. We check this at the estimate rather than guessing.

faq.q: Will a leak under the fridge ruin a vinyl plank floor?
faq.a: It will not ruin the plank. Water that sits for days can find a click seam and dampen the subfloor, so a long-running hidden leak still means lifting a few planks to dry underneath. Rigid core planks click apart and go back together, which is much easier than replacing damaged hardwood.
